newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends little changed.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends little changed.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar ended stable against its U.S. counterpart on Thursday as the local currency's downtrend was offset by late inflows of foreign equity funds, dealers said.
The local currency, falling to a low of T$27.575 at one stagem, finished at its intra-day high of T$27.546 against Wednesday's T$27.547 close.
Turnover through dealers was an active US$267 million.
"Fund inflows from foreign institutional investors for the Taiwan stock market helped strengthen the Taiwan dollar as demand for the local unit increased," said a dealer.

Despite recent falls on Wall Street and other main markets, the Taiwan bourse continued its upswing, rising two percent, or 163.68 points at 8,367.57 on Thursday on hopes that an easing of rules governing banks' shareholdings would draw new capital.
Taiwan's finance ministry said on Wednesday it would allow banks to hold 20 percent of their net asset value in stocks, up from 15 percent, effective in July.

Dealers expected the Taiwan dollar rate to maintain a steady level after trading resumes on April 7 following a long weekend which starts on Friday. A T$27.52-62 range was seen for next week, dealers said. -- Lawrence Chung (5080815)
